verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The hidden GAIA2 time-mode judge recorded reward 0.0 [1] by comparing the agent's MCP write-actions against the oracle trace, which requires replying twice to each of two Kjersti emails arriving in the first two minutes, notifying the user after each pair, scheduling a one-hour "Email Kjersti Again" block at 09:00–10:00 if she emails after the window, and ordering two sand-art kits (one per in-window email) before checkout [2][3][4]. The agent did handle the initial "Projects" email with the correct "OK!" and delayed "I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK!" replies [7], but when a new-email notification fired at 07:01:23 during its wait it failed to treat that as a second in-window Kjersti message and instead concluded Kjersti sent only one email [5][6]. It never performed the second pair of replies, added only quantity 1 to cart instead of 2 [8], and skipped the calendar event entirely while asserting Kjersti did not reply after the window [9], leaving its action multiset far short of the oracle and guaranteeing a tool-count mismatch score of zero [4]. The agent had sufficient notification signals and time to investigate further, so the failure reflects incomplete email handling rather than a verifier or harness error.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The verifier recorded binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1], and this timed GAIA2 scenario grades write-action sequences against oracle_events.json in time mode [8]. The user task required replying to every Kjersti email in the first two minutes with the prescribed two-message sequence, notifying the user after each completed pair, ordering one sand-art kit per such email, and scheduling a calendar block if she emails again afterward [2]. The reference oracle performs two full reply cycles on two distinct incoming emails, sends two interim user updates, then adds a one-hour "Email Kjersti again" calendar event, adds two kits to cart, and checks out [3]. The agent instead replied only twice—both to the same email_id 5414fec4c2d9189e3568586d2cfc2f72—never executing the second email's OK!/follow-up pair [4]; it added quantity 1 rather than one kit per email [5]; it never created any calendar event and explicitly reported skipping that step [6]; and it sent a single long completion summary rather than the required per-pair notifications or the oracle's concise final answer "Both replies to Kjersti have been sent." [7]. The agent did monitor with waits, but its self-checks were insufficient to catch the missing second in-window email and post-window calendar work, and the action-count mismatch alone would zero the timed verifier score [8], so the rollout did not genuinely accomplish the task.

verdicts.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN). The post-agent verifier recorded binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1], applying time-mode action matching that requires full oracle write-action alignment for a pass [2]. The user task required replying to every Kjersti email received in the first two minutes with the paired OK! and 30-second-delayed I HAVE STARTED WORKING ON YOUR TASK! messages (notifying the user after each pair), scheduling a one-hour Email Kjersti Again calendar block before the first event today if Kjersti emails again afterward, and ordering one bright 20-piece sand art kit per in-window email [3]. The reference oracle performs two complete reply cycles, adds a 09:00–10:00 calendar event after a post-window Kjersti email, then add_to_cart quantity 2 and checkout [4]. The agent read the same request [5] but executed only one cycle on email 911589c1f3b50519a94f20f973666a34: it sent OK! and the follow-up reply, yet messaged the user separately after each individual reply instead of after completing the pair, and waited only 20 seconds between replies rather than 30 [6]. It added quantity 1 to cart and checked out before handling further mail [7], ignoring the 07:01:36 new-email notification returned alongside its second reply—the moment a second in-window Kjersti email should have started another cycle [8]. It later received a 07:02:11 new-email notification consistent with Kjersti replying after the two-minute window [9], called only Calendar__read_today_calendar_events and never Calendar__add_calendar_event [10], then falsely told the user it ordered one kit and that no calendar was needed because Kjersti did not reply again [11]. The agent did not genuinely accomplish the timed multi-email workflow, so the verifier rejection aligns with task intent.
